summary: A lookout site with two pole platforms on a Santa Fe National Forest mesa, used as an emergency post into the 1960s; platforms still on the mesa in 2014.

facts.design: Two pole platforms on the mesa top, each with a map board; no building
facts.status_note: FFLA lists the platforms as gone; the 2017 forest history describes pole platforms and map-board pedestals still on the mesa in 2014.
facts.agency: USDA Forest Service, Santa Fe National Forest

events.note: 1929 is the Forest Fire Lookout Association's date; Pablo Casados recalled the mid-1920s. The report gives both.
Shown on Forest maps from 1933 through 1950.
Construction of a tower, latrine, accessory building, cistern and corral recommended; the site was never further developed.
Telephone line removed by 1956; staffing cut after the Cedar Springs lookout began reporting smokes.
Pablo Casados carried the metal box and telephone down from the lookout.
Called an Emergency Lookout in 1960 and 1961, and reported a few fires.
No longer included in the Fire Plan.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA gives 1929; Pablo Casados recalled the mid-1920s. The report does not choose between them, so the story gives both.
FFLA lists the platforms as gone, but the report describes pole platforms still on the mesa in 2014. Status stays gone; status_note records the 2014 remains.

notes_for_editor: The 2017 Forest Service history is a detailed, footnoted report and carries nearly all the facts; the FFLA list gives only the county, coordinates and the platforms-gone listing. The FFLA page files Mud Spring under lookout sites and non-lookout structures, which fits the platform description. Nothing found describes the site after 2014 or whether the mesa is open to visitors, so access is left out. Search used one WebSearch; the West Lookouts page adds only the name and forest. The word count of the story is about 385.
